lawyer:
Abdul Baset Mazumder with Zainal Abedin, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.3.
parties:
Mohsin Kabir (Rupan) ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.: This petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir alias Rupan prays for issuance of Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents (1) Government of Bangladesh represented by the 'Secretary, Ministry of Works. Urban Development, (2) Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka and (3) Mrs. Khairun Nesa to show cause why the impugned order dated 9.6.91 issued by the respondent No.2 Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka) by his memo No. 14 Shuk-170/85-69 (Annexure C) shall not be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. 

 2. Impugned order contained in Annexure G dated 9.6.91 issued by the respondent No.2, Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, 1st 12 Storied Building, Segun Bagicha, Dhaka reads as follows: 

 By the said order respondent No. 2 informed the petitioner that as the Court of Settlement in case No. 422/87 (Ka-126-Sutrapur, Dhaka) by its judgment dated 19.9.88 declared that Khairunnessa is the rightful Bangladeshi owner of the said house property with the land and the property in question in the facts and circumstances of the case cannot be treated and enlisted as abandoned property within the meaning of PO No. 16 of 1972 Therefore, it is excluded from the list of abandoned property and restored to the possession of the petitioner Khairunnessa irrespective of the actions so far taken by the Govt. in respect of the said house property. 

 It appears that the Abandoned Buildings (supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. LIV of 1985) came into force on 28.11.85. Respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa, a citizen of Bangladesh filed Settlement Court Case No. 422, of 1987 before the Court of Settlement by filing an application under section 7 of the said Ordinance claiming the property as her own property and prayed for release of the property from the 'Ka' list of abandoned property. The petitioner submits in the petition that Respondent Khairunnessa made a false story in the aforesaid settlement case that the property belonged to Sheikh Abdullah who died leaving behind a son Md. Ismail" and daughter Ayesha who inherited the property; that Md. Ismail and all the members of his family were killed by the miscreants after liberation; that Ayesha Bibi eventually became sole heir of the property; that she died in the year 1977 leaving behind her daughter Khairunnessa and that Khairunnessa being the sole owner of the property, the said disputed property should be excluded from the list of abandoned property and that possession of the disputed property should be restored to the' respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa. 

 4. It appears that in the Court of Settlement in Settlement Court Case No. 422 of 1987 the petitioner being merely an allottee tenant of the Government was not made a party and it is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the Government did not inform the petitioner that respondent No. 3 had filed the aforesaid case in the Court of Settlement for release of the disputed property. Annexure A of the application filed by Respondent No. 3 Khairunnessa on 8.7.91 praying for vacating the order of status quo passed on 17.6.91 by the learned Single Judge sitting during the vacation is the judgment dated 19.9.88 passed by the Court of Settlement in favour of Respondent No. 3 which has been accepted by the Government. 

 5. It appears from the application of respondent No. 3 Mrs. Khairunnessa for vacating the order of status quo passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court sitting during vacation on 17 .6.91 that the Court of Settlement by its judgment (Annexure-A to the respondent No. 3's application) on 19.9.88 directing that the case property be excluded from the Ka list of abandoned property and that the unencumbered possession thereof be restored to the petitioner (respondent No. 3) without delay. It further appears that as petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir continued to reside in the said house in spite of the judgment of the Court of Settlement, respondent No. 3 was unable to get possession of the case property and having no other alternative she (respondent No. 3) obtained Rule Nisi (Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989) on 27.2.1990 against the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development to show cause why he shall not be directed to restore possession of holding No. 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, Sutrapur, Dhaka to respondent No. 3 of the present writ petition in pursuance of the judgment and order dated 19.9.1988 passed by the Court of Settlement in Case No. 422/89(Ka-126-Sutrapur, Dhaka). In the said Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 a Division Bench of this Court, inter alia passed the following order: 

 Section 10(6) of the said Ordinance provides: "The decision of the Court of Settlement shall be final and shall be binding on all parties concerned". So the Government respondent being a party to the said case disposed of by the Court of Settlement is bound by the judgment and order as aforesaid in which the Court of Settlement allowed the application of the petitioner in the following terms: 

 "In the result, we allow this application and direct that the case property be excluded from the list of abandoned property and further that unencumbered possession thereof be restored to the petitioner without delay". 

 6. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that he was neither made a party in the settlement case No. 422/87 nor made a party in Writ Petition No. 424/89. In the case of Abdul Khaleq Bains and others Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 1987 BO (AD) 121 it has been held by the Appellate Division as follows: 

 "It appears that the plaintiff-appellant filed the suit for declaration of his title to the property on the ground that the property could not have been declared as abandoned property by the Government. Relief claimed by the plaintiff-appellant is against the Government. If the Government cannot justify the legality of its decision to treat the property as abandoned property, it will be so declared by the Court. It is not understood how the addition of defendant-respondent No. 3 in the suit against whom no relief has been claimed in the suit can be of any use or relevance. It is for the Government alone to justify the order passed by it treating the property as abandoned property. Added defendant-respondent No. 3 has nothing to say either for or against the legality or otherwise of the declaration of the Government treating the property as abandoned property. We, therefore, see no reason for upholding the order of the Court below." 

 "From the facts as stated above, submission made by the learned Counsels and authority cited above by them, it appears that in view of the nature of tenancy of respondent Nos. 6 and 7 respectively separate considerations are required for deciding the question before us. It appears that in the writ petition appellant not only prayed for a declaration that the property was not abandoned property and should, therefore, be released from the list of abandoned properties but also prayed for restoration of possession of the premises thereof in occupation of the respondents-allottees of the Government. If the learned Judges in deciding the writ petition declare the property in question to be not abandoned property, it may consider whether it would also order for restoration of possession to the appellant as against Government allottees who were inducted therein after its inclusion in the list of abandoned properties. So far as respondent No. 6 is concerned the position seems to be clear and also admitted by the appellant that it (Respondent No. 6) has been in occupation of the premises since before the property was included in the list of abandoned properties. Its case is, therefore, separate from respondent No. 7. Whether respondent No. 6 would be ordered to be evicted from the premises after the property is declared to be not abandoned property, this would require some consideration. In the case of respondent No. 7, their continuation in the premises as allottee of Government depends on as long as the property was abandoned property, but when such continuance cannot be prolonged after the declaration is given that the property was no more an abandoned property, respondent No. 7 would have to vacate. This probably may not be the case of respondent No. 6 who is also an allotee of the Government though, in fact, it was in the premises as a tenant under the appellant. In this view of the matter we feel that the discretion exercised by the learned Judges in adding respondent No. 6 as a party in the writ petition cannot be disturbed by us. The addition of respondent No. 7, does not, however, seem to be justified." The said decision in the case of Md. Ayub, BCR 1987 AD 350 has no application in the instant case in view of the admitted fact that the petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir was illegally inducted into the said house by the Government erroneously treating it and listing it as an abandoned property, that the present petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir does not claim that he was a tenant in the house in question from before it was taken over by the Government treating it to be abandoned property either under its true owner or under any other person from before it was taken over by the Government as abandoned property as the petitioner has clearly stated in paragraph 3 of the present petition that after liberation the petitioner by filing an application for allotment of an abandoned house to the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development got allotment and possession of the house in question from the Government as an abandoned house. Since the Court of Settlement has given a decision that the property in question is not an abandoned property, that it is to be delivered to its rightful owner, respondent No. 3, Mrs. Khairunnessa and since the Government has also accepted the said decision, the legal position of the petitioner (Md. Mohsin Kabir) is that he has been illegally inducted into the house by the Government and he does not have any right, title and interest of any sort whatsoever to continue to remain in possession of the case property. In these circumstance the petitioner was neither a necessary party nor a proper party in the Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 or in the Settlement Court Case No. 422/87. 

 8. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner without any basis whatsoever that respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa was not the original owner and that Kaniz Fatima Khatun, wife of Khairunnessa's uncle Md. Ismail who was a non-Bengali-was the original owner. It is also submitted equally without any basis that the respondent No 3, Khairunnessas, in connivance with other respondents collusively arranged aforesaid order of settlement in Case No. 422 of 1987 and the order of the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989. The petitioner is not entitled to raise such disputed questions of fact for decision of this court under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in exercise of its summary and extraordinary jurisdiction. The petitioner has, in fact, only challenged Annexure-G dated 9.6.91 passed by respondent No. 2, Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka asking him to vacate the premises at 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, Sutrapur, Dhaka which we find to be a valid and lawfful order in view of the decision in Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 read with the judgment dated 19.9.88 of the Settlement Court Case No. 422 of 1987.
